observations.statement: MS-123 requires a ProviderNativeMetadataPolicy keyed by provider/model capability, with retain, redact, cross-provider drop, same-account replay, and canonicalize dispositions; it also requires cache keys and model catalog version.

MS-123 makes three behavioral outcomes explicit: incompatible native reasoning blocks are never replayed after provider/model switching, model cache scope includes provider, account, and capability catalog version, and image/tool/reasoning capability gates run before sending.

MS-124 extends ContextEpoch with a ProviderCapabilityEpoch covering source, freshness, account/profile scope, route-imposed limits, dynamic discovery provenance, and a model-switch sanitizer; acceptance requires a stale-catalog warning, honoring lower route limits, and strip-or-block handling with a receipt.

MS-125 defines a ProviderNativeReplayMatrix over reasoning-content presence, signatures, user-first role order, images, tool-result role mapping, and same-delta ordering, with multi-turn route tests and thinking-to-non-thinking model-switch tests.

MS-126 requires an EffortSettlementReceipt carrying requested, policy, and effective-wire effort plus provider field, display, support, transform, fallback, reset, latency-bucket, and replay-rule data, and it must prove a settlement state per provider attempt and per child/subagent.

MS-126 requires a fresh effort settlement on model switch, compaction, resume, or subagent spawn; forbids unsupported xhigh/high from appearing honored; requires display_mismatch diagnostics for lagging GUI labels; and distinguishes pre-first-response stalls from ordinary thinking time.
GUI classification is true for MS-123, MS-125, and MS-126, while MS-124 is classified as a non-GUI backend/orchestration contract.
All four units declare PDS-003 and PNC-001 as dependencies and declare no unblocked units.
All four node compile hints explicitly disable WorkNode and NodeSeed creation.
The units name Models_System plus provider, prompt, account, goal-runtime, and usage documents as implementation surfaces, distributing the contracts across several plan owners.
Each unit's validation_surfaces section names the plan-index and bootstrap-ledger validators, followed by repeated behavioral criteria or test descriptions.

candidate_findings.title: Provider-native metadata policy decisions are not deterministic
candidate_findings.statement: The policy enumerates possible dispositions and capability-gate outcomes but does not specify the typed key/value schema, rule precedence, defaults for missing or stale capability data, redaction/canonicalization transforms, or whether an unknown case must block, drop, or send.
candidate_findings.impact: Different builders can make opposite replay and privacy decisions for the same artifact, including leaking account-scoped metadata or producing provider-invalid payloads while still satisfying the stated high-level criteria.

candidate_findings.title: Overlapping replay authorities have no composition contract
candidate_findings.statement: MS-123 introduces ProviderNativeMetadataPolicy and MS-125 introduces ProviderNativeReplayMatrix over overlapping reasoning, signature, image, role, and replay decisions, but the core does not assign a single authority, evaluation order, merge rule, or conflict resolution rule between them.
candidate_findings.impact: The same message can be retained by one contract and rejected or transformed by the other, creating route-dependent behavior and making replay results non-reproducible.

candidate_findings.title: Provider capability freshness cannot be computed reproducibly
candidate_findings.statement: ProviderCapabilityEpoch names source, freshness, scope, route limits, and discovery provenance, while acceptance only requires a stale static catalog warning; no source-precedence rule, freshness clock or threshold, refresh trigger, cache lifetime, invalidation rule, or concurrent-update behavior is defined.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can disagree on which capability record is authoritative or still usable, so stale or route-inappropriate limits can continue to drive requests despite the warning requirement.

candidate_findings.title: Model-switch sanitizer leaves destructive behavior to builders
candidate_findings.statement: The requirement permits incompatible history to be either stripped or blocked but does not define the compatibility predicate, history granularity, choice between strip and block, operation ordering before send, atomicity, recovery path, or receipt schema and consumer.
candidate_findings.impact: One implementation may silently discard history while another halts the request, causing inconsistent user outcomes, possible context loss, and receipts that cannot be compared or audited.

candidate_findings.title: Effort settlement truth has fields but no determination algorithm
candidate_findings.statement: EffortSettlementReceipt lists fields and possible outcomes such as honored, clamped, ignored, transformed, blocked, reset, and unsupported, but it does not define field types, status enum cardinality, precedence among requested/policy/wire/provider evidence, support-source authority, fallback selection, or reset-detection logic.
candidate_findings.impact: Two implementations can report different effective effort and GUI truth for the same provider attempt, undermining the receipt's stated purpose and allowing unsupported effort to be misrepresented.

candidate_findings.title: Effort settlement lifecycle lacks identity and concurrency semantics
candidate_findings.statement: Fresh settlements are required for model switch, compaction, resume, and subagent spawn, but no receipt identity, attempt/child correlation key, event ordering, idempotency, deduplication, persistence, retention, inheritance, or concurrent-transition rule is specified.
candidate_findings.impact: Overlapping lifecycle events can attach a stale or duplicate settlement to the wrong provider attempt or child, producing incorrect diagnostics and irreconcilable audit history.

candidate_findings.title: First-response latency and stall classification are not reproducible
candidate_findings.statement: The receipt includes first_response_latency_bucket and acceptance requires pre-first-token/reasoning stalls to be typed separately, but the contract does not define bucket boundaries, clock origin, terminal event, streaming phase, timeout boundary, or classification for partial provider output.
candidate_findings.impact: Latency and stall evidence will vary by implementation and transport, preventing reliable comparison, alerting, and acceptance decisions.

candidate_findings.title: P0 behavioral acceptance lacks executable evidence oracles
candidate_findings.statement: The validation surfaces provide two validator commands and otherwise repeat behavior statements; the replay unit names tests without specifying a harness, fixtures, provider/model/route versions, expected serialized outputs, receipt assertions, negative cases, or pass/fail evidence format.
candidate_findings.impact: Plan and ledger validation can succeed without proving runtime replay, sanitizer, capability, or effort behavior, so these P0 contracts cannot be certified consistently from the named evidence.

candidate_findings.title: MS-123 acceptance omits several required policy outcomes
candidate_findings.statement: The canonical obligation covers signatures, reasoning IDs, nullable content, model variants, image/video content, provider account scoping, redaction, canonicalization, and same-account replay, while acceptance only checks incompatible reasoning replay, cache scope, and image/tool/reasoning capability gates.
candidate_findings.impact: An implementation can pass every stated MS-123 acceptance criterion without demonstrating safe signature handling, nullable or video behavior, account replay isolation, redaction, or canonicalization.

candidate_findings.title: GUI truth and accessibility consumers are not specified
candidate_findings.statement: Three units are marked GUI-related and MS-126 constrains a GUI label and diagnostic flag, but the core does not identify the screen or component, visible states, user actions, accessibility exposure, localization behavior, diagnostic discoverability, or redaction rules.
candidate_findings.impact: Required truth may be hidden in diagnostics, presented inconsistently, or inaccessible even when backend receipts are correct.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: The metadata-policy contract explicitly enumerates retain, redact, cross-provider drop, same-account replay, and canonicalize as required disposition categories and explicitly includes cache keys and model catalog version.
Provider/model switching, cache isolation, and pre-send capability checks have explicit acceptance outcomes rather than being left entirely implicit.
The capability-epoch unit explicitly requires lower route-imposed context limits to win and requires a receipt when incompatible history is stripped or blocked.

The replay matrix explicitly names reasoning-content required/forbidden state, signatures, role order, images, tool-result mapping, and same-delta ordering, and it names both multi-turn route replay and model-switch test classes.
The effort contract explicitly distinguishes requested, policy, and effective-wire effort and requires per-attempt and per-child/subagent settlement truth.
MS-126 explicitly prevents unsupported xhigh/high from displaying as honored, specifies display_mismatch for lagging GUI labels, and separates pre-first-response stalls from ordinary thinking time.
The planning compile boundary is explicit in every unit's node hint: WorkNodes and NodeSeeds are not created.

unknowns.statement: The assigned core does not reveal the exact schemas, enums, defaults, precedence, or conflict-resolution mechanism for ProviderNativeMetadataPolicy and ProviderNativeReplayMatrix.
The assigned core does not reveal which capability source is authoritative, how freshness is calculated, or when a ProviderCapabilityEpoch is refreshed or invalidated.
The assigned core does not reveal the model-switch compatibility predicate, when stripping is allowed instead of blocking, or how users and consumers recover stripped history from its receipt.
The assigned core does not reveal EffortSettlementReceipt identity, persistence, retention, ordering, child-parent correlation, or the algorithm that turns provider evidence into settlement status.
The assigned core does not reveal the GUI destinations, accessibility semantics, or user-visible recovery actions for replay, capability, and effort outcomes.
The assigned core does not reveal an executable behavioral harness, immutable fixture set, expected receipt snapshots, or evidence format for proving the named acceptance criteria.
